extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in media watchdogs, media literacy, and journalism criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, definitions, and practices used by (and critiques of) Project Censored for identifying, curating, and publishing 'under-reported' or 'censored' news stories, including pedagogical methods and editorial dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junk food news / newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate media often featured trivial and non-newsworthy stories rather than covering newsworthy issues — Jensen termed this 'junk food news'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Censored's early work and chapters in its yearbooks expose examples of 'junk food news' to argue that newsroom choices deprioritize important reporting; the concept is used as a standard to judge whether media coverage is substantively important rather than trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Under-reported / 'Censored' story selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Censored publishes an annual listing of the most significant but under-reported news stories (the 'Censored' lists / yearbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top 'Censored' news stories are identified through the Campus Affiliates Program and archived on Project Censored's website; the annual book and related media (radio program, events) disseminate the selected stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: "News abuse" refers to corporate media stories that were newsworthy, but presented in a slanted or non-newsworthy manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Censored added the concept of 'News Abuse' to elaborate on 'junk food news' — used as a criterion to evaluate not just whether an item was covered but how fairly and usefully it was presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology accuracy: appropriate use of 'censorship'
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that Project Censored uses the term 'censorship' broadly to mean under-reporting rather than governmentally imposed suppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commentators (e.g., William Powers) argue that labeling under-reporting as 'censorship' is misleading; the implied standard is to reserve 'censorship' for governmental or explicit suppression and be precise in terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process validity and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about a 'dubious selection process' and controversies (e.g., judge resignations) indicate that selection procedures should be rigorous, transparent, and free of conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques (Don Hazen; resignation of two judges over a keynote speaker decision) suggest Project Censored ought to demonstrate clear, defensible methods for choosing items and avoid practices that reinforce bias or self-marginalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of under-reporting / factual basis for 'under-reported' claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics note that some items Project Censored labeled as under-reported had appeared in major outlets (e.g., The New York Times), suggesting the need to verify claims of under-reporting before labeling a story 'censored'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard implied is to check breadth and prominence of prior coverage and document evidence that a story was indeed neglected in mainstream reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and avoidance of denialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Censored has been criticized (e.g., New Politics magazine) for denying or minimizing documented atrocities (Serbian war crimes), signaling that factual accuracy is a core evaluative standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections and commentary should adhere to established historical facts and mainstream evidentiary standards; inclusion of revisionist or denialist claims undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational outreach and media literacy emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Censored's stated mission is to 'educate students and the public about the importance of a truly free press' and to focus on student media literacy and critical thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work produced under the Project is expected to have pedagogical value: fostering critical thinking, media literacy, and public education about press freedoms (e.g., Campus Affiliates Program activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative campus-based identification (Campus Affiliates Program)
rubrics_metrics.description: Top 'Censored' stories are identified through a collaborative effort between faculty and students at many colleges and universities via the Campus Affiliates Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implied criterion is academic collaboration and student-faculty involvement in nominating, reviewing, and validating candidate stories as part of the selection methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination formats (yearbook, radio, events, documentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Censored produces an annual book, a weekly radio program, public events, and has been the subject of documentaries to disseminate its findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for presenting selected stories include curating material for yearbooks, radio, and public programming and archiving lists on the website; past co-publishing arrangements and documentary screenings are examples of dissemination practices to reach wider audiences.
